items.expected-result: `serve --port 0` binds and reports its port; `serve --restart` on that port cycles the server it finds rather than attaching, and never touches port 7721
items.evidence: Now listening on: http://127.0.0.1:63911 | pid on 63911 before restart = 33887 | after `serve --restart --port 63911` the incumbent is gone | lsof 7721 still pid=98602 (the user's own server) throughout
items.observed-result: serve --port 0 binds an ephemeral port and reports it; serve --restart cycles the server it finds on that port. Never touched 7721.
items.acceptation-reason: Restart is a FOREGROUND server, not a fire-and-forget command — it replaces the incumbent and then serves. An invocation that blocks is correct behaviour, not a hang; worth knowing before someone 'fixes' it.

items.expected-result: memory_write returns a hash for a stored entry; a rejected write returns Stored=false with a reason and no fabricated hash (ADR-0032)
items.observed-result: A real content hash and stored:true — no sentinel hash, no fabricated entry.
items.acceptation-reason: ADR-0032's honest write outcome holds on the shipped build.

items.expected-result: memory_search returns the written entry through hybrid BM25 + vector RRF ranking
items.command: tools/call memory_search {projectId:"checklist", query:"read path findable by search readable by hash", scope:"all"}
items.evidence: 2 results; ranking 1 and 0.9853372434017593; both carry sourceFile "docs/checklist-probe.md" with chunkIndex/totalChunks 0/2
items.observed-result: Both written entries returned and ranked. Note 0.98533 is NOT the pure (k+1)/(k+rank)=0.98387, which corroborates the review's corrected finding that SourceAffinityRanker perturbs the score after fusion.
items.acceptation-reason: Retrieval works FTS-only here: no embedding provider is configured on a fresh root, so vector recall is untested by this item — see memory-get item's note.

items.evidence: End processing HTTP request after 7.077ms - 401 | ai-raccoon: the backend at http://127.0.0.1:7721/mcp would not open a session (401 Unauthorized ... does not match the token in /Users/arasz/.ai-raccoon/mcp-token) — check that <scratch>/mcp-token holds the token it minted | `ai-raccoon --help` Commands: access, model, retrieval, sweep, noise, queryguard, sync, ingest, watch, encryption, extract, maintenance, serve  (no `settings`)
items.observed-result: The unrecognised verb did not error. It fell through to the proxy launch path, which dialled the DEFAULT port 7721 — the user's live server — and failed on a token mismatch against the live install's token file. A command explicitly scoped to a scratch --data-root reached into the production install.

This run reproduces it on the shipped 1.13.0 build and RAISES its consequence — the lane described a mistyped verb hanging or attaching to a backend; it also crosses data roots, so a scratch-scoped command is not scratch-scoped.
